messages:
eve_acme: hi — spike just hit our API around 11:07 UTC and we started getting lots of 429s with error quota_exceeded. Were on Dedicated with reserved capacity, so surprised org-level quota would be applied. Traffic came from thousands of client IPs (post-deploy surge). attaching a sample response header from a client curl:

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-scope: org
x-rate-limit-limit: 60000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1678904020
x-client-ip: 22.33.44.55
x-api-key-prefix: sk_prod_abc123
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "quota_exceeded",
  "message": "Org quota exhausted"
}
```

Could this be proxy IP scoping gone wrong? Our clients are behind many NATs. Were a bit panicked, any help?

alice_support: thanks Eve :wave: — sorry about that. Can you confirm org id and project id and whether these requests hit the public API endpoint or a private VPC? Also paste the full response headers (x-request-id if possible). Well triage.

eve_acme: org=acme-42 project=web-sdk env=prod. endpoint=https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate. sample curl we used: 

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_prod_abc123" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate

alice_support: got it. pinging SRE.

ratebot: alert: org acme-42 exceeded org monthly input_token quota threshold at 2026-03-15T11:06:12Z — creating ticket #INC-9281

ben_sre: quick notes — org-level quota is aggregated across all projects and ties to the billing/commit. Dedicated reserved capacity guarantees GPU throughput but does not automatically increase token allowances at the org accounting layer. If a simultaneous burst from many clients occurred, org token accounting can show exhaustion even if Dedicated pool has capacity.

ben_sre: also worth noting: proxy/IP scoping influences enforcement. If requests are seen as coming from lots of distinct IPs vs a single proxy, that changes which limit (ip vs project vs org) is hit.

ben_sre: can you run this from one affected host and paste the headers you get?

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_prod_abc123" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health

and paste x-rate-limit-* headers.

eve_acme: did that, here's one response I just grabbed:

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rate-limit-scope: project
x-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1971234800
x-api-key-prefix: sk_prod_abc123
x-proxy-ip: 34.56.78.90

alice_support: interesting — some responses show scope=org and others scope=project. That suggests mixed routing: some entry nodes are applying org-level enforcement (likely hitting the org quota gate), others project-level. We'll check routing logs. In the meantime, mitigation options:
1) rotate the API key to force new routing (temporary)
2) request an emergency org token uplift (we can apply one-time credit)
3) enable per-key/project burst windows if your plan supports it.

carlos_prod: adding context — we recently deployed a CDN in front of clients that changed X-Forwarded-For behavior; that may have altered proxy grouping so upstream attributes requests differently. Ben, any change to grouping logic on our side?

ben_sre: no grouping changes on platform side recently. Note: on Mar 14 we did a fix to prefer signed X-Forwarded-For when present; unsigned xfwd may be ignored and we fall back to source IP. If your CDN started signing the header (or changed header order), that could flip grouping semantics.

eve_acme: CDN sends X-Forwarded-For with original IP and also CF-Connecting-IP. I can paste a sample header block.

alice_support: for immediate relief we applied a +2M token one-time org uplift (INC-9281) — should be live in 2–3 min. Also enabled a short grace window to reduce 429s while we investigate. Please verify traffic.

eve_acme: seeing far fewer 429s now, thanks! Will upload traffic dump and timeline for PM. Any recommended long-term fix?

ben_sre: long-term options: 
- increase org token commit to cover expected spikes (billing change)
- enable per-project reserved bursts so a noisy project doesn't exhaust org tokens
- normalize proxy headers at CDN edge so upstream grouping is stable

Also: if you create many API keys under the same org and rotate them rapidly, consider per-key quotas to limit aggregate risk.

alice_support: keeping INC-9281 open and assigning to eng-sre for follow-up and postmortem. tagging @carlos_prod for action items. :eyes: 

eve_acme: appreciated — will prepare timeline + logs and reach out for the PM.
